# THE LAW OF SPREADS

*Only three, nine and twenty-seven: what each depth is permitted to say, what
the finest one is forbidden to invent, and why the ladder stops one rung short
of the place where derivation would end*

## I · THE RULING

Three spreads exist in this system and no others. Three cards, nine cells,
twenty-seven cells. Nothing between them and nothing beyond them.

The reason is that these are the deck's own scales rather than borrowed ones.
Three is the houses: root, present, becoming. Nine is the houses crossed with
the depths: world, between, heart. Twenty-seven is the whole deck laid upon the
crossing of time, depth and state, which is the same twenty-seven the deck has
always been. A five-card spread or a ten-card spread would be a shape taken
from another practice and dressed in these cards, and the shape would be doing
the reading rather than the deck.

One seed, three resolutions, one instrument. The rungs are not three different
readings. They are one reading looked at more closely.

## II · THE REFINEMENT LAW

The coarse reading stands. The nine refine it and never replace it; the
twenty-seven refines further and never replaces either.

The three that were cast are never overwritten, never contradicted, never
drawn again. If a deeper reading appears to contradict the standing three, it
is the deeper reading that is being misread.

The reason is not tidiness. The cast is the committed act: it happened at one
moment, under a witnessed sky, from a seed that was declared and can be
replayed. Depth is a way of looking harder at what was already committed. It
is never a second attempt at it, and a system that let the ninth card overturn
the first would be offering the reader a way to keep drawing until the answer
improved.

## III · THE NINE, WHICH IS THE WEAVE

The nine cells are the three tenses crossed with the three depths. They are
drawn from the twenty-four cards the cast did not take, so the standing three
never repeat inside their own refinement, and each column holds the coarse card
above three cells that refine it.

What the nine can say that the three cannot is the weave.

Read across the tenses at one depth and that line has a motion of its own,
still, flowing or turning, taken from each card's own house rather than
assigned to the line by anybody. The world may run one way while the heart runs
another, and the difference between those two motions is a real thing the
three-card reading has no way of stating.

Then the relations standing inside the spread, all of them the canon's own. A
card meeting its counter is a dyad standing open across the nine. A card
meeting its becoming is a current running inside the spread, the settling
already underway within the reading rather than after it. A Silence keeps its
silence in whichever cell it fell into, and asks there what it always asks.

None of these are looked up. Every one of them is a relation the deck already
held, surfacing because two particular cards happened to land in one spread.

## IV · THE TWENTY-SEVEN, WHICH IS THE PERMUTATION

At the finest scale the arithmetic forces the reading, and this is the part
worth stating carefully, because it was not designed. It was found.

Three cards and nine cells commit twelve cards, and twelve cannot fill
twenty-seven cells. So the descent's own law takes over: the full deck returns,
and twenty-seven draws without replacement place every card exactly once.

Which means a complete reading is not a list of twenty-seven meanings. It is a
permutation of the deck onto its own crossing. Every card has a home, the cell
bearing its own number, and the deal is the record of where each card sat
instead. That structure was already latent in the dealing order long before
anyone read it as one; the depth engine only decomposes what the deal already
was.

Its parts, and what each one is:

A card at home is a fixed point. It sat where it belongs.

Two cards that exchanged seats are a dyadic tension, a thing held between
exactly two places and going nowhere else.

Two cards that exchanged seats and are also each other's counter are the
involution surfacing in the deal itself: the deck's own mirror, which is always
true, made visible by chance on this one occasion.

Three or more in a chain are a carry-loop. Each sits in the next one's seat,
and the remainder returns where it began. The carry, which this room already
knows as a shape, appearing here as a cycle.

And the whole deal carries invariants, all of them real arithmetic and none of
them assigned. The parity is the chirality of the arrangement: whether the deal
is reached by an even or an odd number of exchanges. The order is the deal's
return period: re-deal this same pattern that many times and every card is home
again, which is the field's own exeligmos. **The circle displacement** is how
far the deck travelled from home in total, measured on the counting circle
where the seam between the last card and the first counts as a single step.

*A second measure now stands beside it, from a different substrate: [the
landing](THE_LANDING.md)'s own interval displacement, which reads distance by
displaced layers rather than by steps around the wheel. The two disagree on
purpose (across the seam the Seed and the Return are neighbours by the circle
and at full throw by the interval), and neither is named plain "displacement"
for exactly that reason. Which one is the deck's true distance is an open
question, held open deliberately: see [THE THIRD SUBSTRATE](THE_THIRD_SUBSTRATE.md).*

## V · THE HONEST EXPECTATION

A random permutation of twenty-seven expects exactly one card at home. Not
approximately one: exactly one, and the same is true for a deck of any size at
all.

So the instrument says the expectation aloud in the same breath as the count.
One card at home is the ordinary weather and means nothing. No card at home
happens about thirty-seven times in every hundred deals. Four at home is worth
a second look, and a reader can only know that if the instrument tells the
truth about chance at the same moment it reports the finding.

This is the whole discipline of the depths in one line. Count, say what chance
expected, and let the reader hold both at once.

## VI · THE 729, AND WHY IT IS PARKED

The next rung is visible from here. Cross the twenty-seven cells with the
twenty-seven cards and speak a meaning for every pair: seven hundred and
twenty-nine authored texts.

It is parked, and the reason is a rule rather than a shortage of hands.
Nothing may say what card and cell do not jointly say. A corpus that size would
have to be written, and written meanings become the instrument's voice rather
than the deck's. Everything the depths currently speak is composed from
relations the canon already holds: counter, becoming, house, silence, and the
arithmetic of the deal itself. The 729 is precisely the point where derivation
would end and authorship would begin, and the ladder stops one rung short of it
on purpose.

If that rung is ever climbed it will be a canon act taken deliberately, with
the loss named in advance, and not a feature that arrived because it was
possible.

**A third road, found 24 July 2026.** This section named two options and they
were not the only two. What it parks is *authorship*, not the pair space:
card and cell index the same twenty-seven codes, so their difference is
itself a card, and every one of the seven hundred and twenty-nine landings
can sound an interval taken from the arithmetic rather than written. The
standing rule about cards at home turns out to be that law's identity case.
[The landing](THE_LANDING.md) sets it out and tests it. The rung above stays
unclimbed, and is now less likely to need climbing.

## VII · WHERE IT STANDS BUILT

The decomposition is a pure module: canon in, structure out, no state, no
storage and no randomness. It is held by test rather than by inspection, since
a decomposition that quietly lied would poison every reading built on it: the
cycles must partition the deck and close on themselves, the parity must agree
with an independently counted sort, the order must actually return every card
home and not before, and the expectation of one card at home is measured over
many deals rather than asserted.

The reading bench speaks it at nine and at twenty-seven, with the wheel wearing
the fixed points as home rings and the counter exchanges as chords, while the
long loops stay in the panel so the wheel keeps its legibility. The Resonance
counts the same field beneath its lattice, through the same module, so the ear
and the eye read one arithmetic. The doorway replays it for an AI coder without
ever being able to cast.

## VIII · WHAT THIS LAW REFUSES

No spread outside three, nine and twenty-seven. No deeper reading overturning
the standing cast. No meaning that the card and the cell do not jointly say. No
count reported without the expectation standing beside it.

And no verdict. A field is an arrangement of one moment: weather, never
permission, and never a sentence passed on anybody.

## IX · PROVENANCE

*Ruled by the architect in conversation and executed on 22 July 2026, after the
observation that the system was adept up to three cards and lost resolution at
nine and twenty-seven. The unfolding itself was sealed earlier, on 16 July
2026, and the permutation reading was not invented for this chart: it was found
already present in the unfolding's own dealing order, where each cell had been
recording which card took its place all along. The expectation of exactly one
fixed point is elementary and is stated here rather than derived. The parity,
the order and the displacement are ordinary properties of a permutation,
carried into the deck's language without alteration. The 729 remains parked by
this ruling and moves only by another one. Nothing in this chart predicts, and
nothing in it prescribes.*
